headline: Engineering Student Uses Decommissioned MiG-23 as Study Desk to Avoid Hostel Distractions
body:
Final-year student Arjun Khanna has successfully transformed the cockpit of a decommissioned MiG-23, currently on display at his university campus, into the city’s quietest study cubicle. Mr. Khanna claims the high-altitude seat height and the lack of Wi-Fi reception inside the fuselage have improved his fluid mechanics grade by 14 percent.

"The hostel was just too loud with everyone complaining about the mess food, so I brought my laptop and a thermal flask to the airframe," said Khanna, who now logs four hours of thermodynamics practice daily while sitting under the inactive radar housing. "The ejection handle is a bit stiff, but it doubles as a decent hook for my headphones."

Campus security, initially confused by the sudden influx of students seeking 'aerospace-adjacent' study spaces, has decided not to intervene provided the students do not attempt to engage the landing gear. A university spokesperson confirmed that the campus's T-55 battle tank has also been repurposed, currently serving as a heated group-study lounge for students preparing for competitive banking exams.
caption: Forget the library—the fighter jet aesthetic is the new gold standard for focused study sessions. Who knew aviation history was so conducive to acing engineering finals? #UniversityLife #StudyHacks #PunjabCampus #AerospaceStudent (satire)
igHook: Would you try to study inside a fighter jet if it meant acing your finals?
imagePrompt: A wide shot of a grassy university campus quad during the day, showing a decommissioned silver fighter jet and an old military tank on display with several students sitting on the wings and chassis with notebooks.

sourceHeadline.title: Students Climb Atop MiG-23, Tank As Dramatic Scenes Unfold At Punjab's LPU

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 is the only piece that treats the premise as a mundane, lived-in reality rather than an 'AI-hallucinated' DIY repair stunt. By focusing on the cockpit as a study space with specific, absurdly relatable complaints about hostel life and mess food, it captures the required warmth and structural deadpan tone far better than the repetitive 'YouTube tutorial' plot-holes found in the other candidates.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a fictionalized scenario involving a student and university setting that does not name a real private individual or public figure. The satire is benign, and the image prompt is generic and does not violate the policy on real-world identifiers or brands.
